test.//dependsOn: The default lane is now purely in-process source-level unit tests. The 23 resource-consuming suites (real subprocess spawns of the built dist/index.js, real python/JVM hosts, real HTTP servers, and the CPU-heavy real-extraction suites) moved to sibling *.e2e.ts files with cheap *.spec.ts stubs, so this target no longer spawns the built artifact or a JVM and no longer declares `build` / `apigen-java:package`; those resource prerequisites now live ONLY on the `e2e` target below. This target inherits the workspace targetDefaults.test dependsOn (["lint", "^build"]).
test.//inputs: Exclude *.e2e.ts so editing a resource-consuming suite never invalidates the default lane's cache — it never runs those files (its vitest `include` is `src/**/*.spec.ts`, see vite.config.ts). Mirrors the workspace targetDefaults.test inputs plus the negative pattern.

e2e.//: RESOURCE-CONSUMING lane. Deliberately NOT part of `affected` and NOT referenced by any target's dependsOn or by targetDefaults — it runs ONLY on an explicit `nx run apigen-cli:e2e` (and nx affected never selects it). It runs the sibling *.e2e.ts suites via vitest.e2e.config.ts. `dependsOn` is exactly the resource prerequisites those suites need: `build` (most spawn the built dist/index.js) and `apigen-java:package` (java-ts-decimal-parity drives the JVM).
